title: HTTP Protocol
description: HTTP reference covering messages, methods, status codes, headers, content negotiation, caching, conditional requests, authentication, cookies, CORS, security, streaming, proxies, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, and diagnostics.

subtopics.title: Requests, Responses & Representations
subtopics.description: HTTP exchanges metadata and optional bodies. A resource is identified by a URI; its representation is selected by method, headers, authorization, and negotiation.

codeBlocks.code:
GET /users/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: application/json

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: private, max-age=60

{"id":42,"name":"Ada"}

subtopics.title: Methods, Safety & Idempotency
subtopics.description: Safe methods are read-oriented; idempotent methods may be repeated with the same intended effect. Retry policy must also consider body replayability and application idempotency.

callouts.title: Use Idempotency Keys for Retried Creates
callouts.text: For payment or creation POSTs, bind a client-generated key to one canonical result and define retention/conflict behavior.

subtopics.title: Status Code Selection
subtopics.description: Choose codes by protocol semantics, not framework convenience, and return a stable machine-readable error body.

codeBlocks.code:
200 OK / 201 Created + Location / 202 Accepted
204 No Content / 304 Not Modified
400 malformed / 401 authenticate / 403 forbidden / 404 absent
409 conflict / 412 precondition / 422 semantic input
429 rate limited + Retry-After / 500 fault / 503 unavailable

callouts.title: 401 and 403 Differ
callouts.text: 401 means valid authentication credentials are required; 403 means the server understood the identity but refuses authorization.

subtopics.title: Content Type, Encoding & Negotiation
subtopics.description: Content-Type describes the body; Accept requests media types; Content-Encoding describes compression; Vary tells caches which request headers selected the response.

codeBlocks.code:
Accept: application/json
Accept-Encoding: br, gzip
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Encoding: br
Vary: Accept-Encoding, Origin

subtopics.title: Cache-Control, ETag & Preconditions
subtopics.description: Freshness avoids revalidation; validators make stale checks cheap; preconditions prevent lost updates.

codeBlocks.code:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=30
ETag: "user-42-v7"

If-None-Match: "user-42-v7"  # GET -> 304
If-Match: "user-42-v7"       # update -> 412 if changed

callouts.title: Caching Authenticated Data Requires Deliberate Policy
callouts.text: Use private/no-store where appropriate and ensure shared caches cannot serve one user's representation to another.

subtopics.title: Authorization, Cookies & CSRF
subtopics.description: TLS protects transport; authentication establishes identity; authorization checks the action and resource. Cookie credentials require SameSite and CSRF design.

codeBlocks.code:
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Set-Cookie: session=<opaque>; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

callouts.title: Never Put Credentials in URLs
callouts.text: URLs leak through logs, browser history, analytics, referrers, and screenshots. Use headers or secure cookies.

subtopics.title: CORS, Origins & Preflight
subtopics.description: CORS is a browser read-permission protocol, not server authentication. Allow exact origins, methods, and headers; credentialed requests cannot use wildcard origin.

codeBlocks.code:
OPTIONS /orders HTTP/1.1
Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST

Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Vary: Origin

subtopics.title: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 & HTTP/3
subtopics.description: Semantics remain mostly stable while framing and transport change: HTTP/2 multiplexes binary streams over TCP; HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP and avoids cross-stream TCP head-of-line blocking.

table.title: HTTP Version Comparison
rows: Header compression; one TCP loss can delay streams
Faster migration/handshake potential; infrastructure support required

subtopics.title: Streaming, Proxies & Diagnostics
subtopics.description: Account for reverse proxies, forwarded headers, buffering, body limits, deadlines, retries, trace context, and connection reuse.

codeBlocks.code:
curl -v --compressed https://api.example.com/health
curl -I https://example.com/asset.js
curl --http2 -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://example.com

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Set TLS, body/header limits, timeouts, cache policy, idempotent retry rules, CORS/CSRF policy, request IDs, structured errors, rate limits, and proxy trust explicitly.
